notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Map the service business before starting the conversation.
intro: A proposed market-development workbench for Avoca: research service brands, locations and operating context, then prepare a grounded front-office discovery handoff.
queueIntro: All service businesses and operating scenarios are fictional. No consumer contact records, call recordings or homeowner information appear in the demo.
workbenchIntro: Review account structure, business-contact provenance and the call-handling question. A research score does not prove missed calls, booking problems or revenue opportunity.
firstBody: Connect the operating brand, trade and service footprint to a credible call or booking question, an appropriate business contact and an owned next step.

fields.label: Service brand, locations and parent resolved
Call or booking workflow question is evidence-based
Professional business contact and provenance checked
Campaign quality and suppression checks complete
Reply and meeting handoff owner assigned

rules.title: Resolve the service-business account
rules.next: Keep the operating brand, branch and parent relationship distinct before assigning an outbound account.

rules.title: Verify the service footprint
rules.next: Use supported service categories and geography instead of assuming every branch serves the same area.

rules.title: Write the front-office discovery question
rules.next: Ask how the business handles calls or booking. Do not assert missed-call volume or lost revenue without evidence.

rules.title: Verify the business contact
rules.next: Use a sourced professional route to the appropriate operating role, not consumer records or guessed addresses.

rules.title: Review outbound quality before launch
rules.next: Check account duplication, stop requests and the agreed sending policy. Do not treat volume as a success measure.

rules.title: Assign the revenue handoff
rules.next: A positive reply or scheduled meeting needs an owner; keep booked meetings separate from held qualified discovery.

ready.title: Ready for service-business discovery review
ready.next: The seller can inspect the company context and ask how the front office works. Actual call volume, booking performance and product fit remain discovery questions.

experiments.name: Trade-specific front-office discovery
experiments.hypothesis: A relevant operating question improves qualified conversations.
experiments.treatment: Trade and footprint context with a booking question
experiments.primary: Qualified held meetings per starting account
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Location-aware account deduplication
experiments.hypothesis: Brand and parent mapping reduces overlapping prospecting.
experiments.treatment: Operating brand, location and parent keys
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Define the service-business market map
roadmap.body: Agree on brand, branch and parent keys, priority trades and acceptable research sources.

roadmap.title: Pilot a quality-controlled motion
roadmap.body: Build sourced briefs and business-contact review. Align reply suppression and seller ownership before launch.
roadmap.measure: Relevant replies and correctly owned next steps

roadmap.title: Improve qualified conversion
roadmap.body: Compare trade and channel cohorts through held discovery and qualified pipeline. Train the team on corrections and failure recovery.

metricsTitle: A booked meeting is a step, not the outcome.
metricsIntro: Synthetic cohort for a location-aware outbound pilot.
metricsNotes: All numbers are illustrative and do not describe Avoca or its customers.
Track brand-level and location-level counts separately to avoid overstating market coverage.
Stop requests and active relationships take priority over any new prospecting proposal.
